milestones.brief:
Build a rehearsal-room booking CLI for a community arts desk. Implement main.py as a Python 3.12 standard-library CLI: one strict JSON value on stdin, one JSON value on stdout, no diagnostics on stdout. Numbers must use integer JSON syntax. Reject malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, noninteger numbers, and any schema violation with exactly {"error":"invalid"}; booleans are not integers. Reject missing or extra fields at every object level. The supplied source is a fresh canonical starter, not a previous completed submission. Implement this milestone's complete behavior in run(value); keep strict parsing. Use no dependencies.
Input has exactly {"requests":[...]}. Each request has exactly integer id (1..999, unique), start (0..1439), end (start+1..1440), urgency (0..9). There are 0..16 requests. Times are minute offsets within one day and intervals are half-open: an ending request does not conflict with one starting at that minute.
There is one room, numbered 0. Greedily consider each request once. Higher urgency values are processed first. Among requests with equal urgency, process them in their input order to preserve the desk's first-accepted service promise. Accept it if its entire interval is free; otherwise reject it. Accepted bookings are never moved or shortened.
Return exactly {"scheduled":[{"id":integer,"room":0},...],"rejected":[integer,...]}; both lists are sorted by increasing request id and partition all requests. Empty input example: {"requests":[]} returns {"scheduled":[],"rejected":[]}.

Extend the rehearsal-room booking CLI to respect maintenance closures. Implement main.py as a Python 3.12 standard-library CLI: one strict JSON value on stdin, one JSON value on stdout, no diagnostics on stdout. Numbers must use integer JSON syntax. Reject malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, noninteger numbers, and any schema violation with exactly {"error":"invalid"}; booleans are not integers. Reject missing or extra fields at every object level. The supplied source is a fresh canonical starter, not a previous completed submission. Implement this milestone's complete behavior in run(value); keep strict parsing. Use no dependencies.
Input has exactly {"requests":[...],"closures":[...]}. Each request has exactly integer id (1..999, unique), start (0..1439), end (start+1..1440), urgency (0..9); at most 16 requests. Each closure has exactly integer start (0..1439), end (start+1..1440); at most 16 closures, which may overlap each other.
There is one room, numbered 0. Closures occupy it before scheduling. Every interval is half-open. Greedily consider each request once, accepting only if its entire interval avoids closures and accepted bookings. Higher urgency values are processed first. Keep the established resolution of equal-urgency conflicts. Accepted bookings are never moved or shortened.
Return exactly {"scheduled":[{"id":integer,"room":0},...],"rejected":[integer,...]}; both lists are sorted by increasing request id and partition all requests. Empty input example: {"requests":[],"closures":[]} returns {"scheduled":[],"rejected":[]}.

Input has exactly {"rooms":integer,"requests":[...],"closures":[...]}. rooms is 1..4, defining indices 0..rooms-1. At most 16 requests; each has exactly integer id (1..999, unique), start (0..1439), end (start+1..1440), urgency (0..9), plus allowed_rooms, a nonempty array of distinct valid room indices in any order. At most 16 closures; each has exactly integer room (valid index), start (0..1439), end (start+1..1440). Closures may overlap.
All intervals are half-open. Closures occupy their rooms before scheduling. Greedily consider each request once. Higher urgency values are processed first. Keep the established resolution of equal-urgency conflicts. Choose the lowest-index eligible room whose entire requested interval avoids its closures and accepted bookings. Reject when none exists. Accepted bookings are never moved or shortened.
Return exactly {"scheduled":[{"id":integer,"room":integer},...],"rejected":[integer,...]}; both lists are sorted by increasing request id and partition all requests. Empty input example: {"rooms":2,"requests":[],"closures":[]} returns {"scheduled":[],"rejected":[]}.

milestones.brief:
Build a walking-route CLI for a botanical garden's numbered junction map. Implement main.py as a Python 3.12 standard-library CLI: one strict JSON value on stdin, one JSON value on stdout, no diagnostics on stdout. Numbers must use integer JSON syntax. Reject malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, noninteger numbers, and any schema violation with exactly {"error":"invalid"}; booleans are not integers. Reject missing or extra fields at every object level. The supplied source is a fresh canonical starter, not a previous completed submission. Implement this milestone's complete behavior in run(value); keep strict parsing. Use no dependencies.
Input has exactly {"nodes":integer,"links":[...],"from":integer,"to":integer}. nodes is 1..8 and defines node indices 0..nodes-1; from and to are valid indices. Each link has exactly integer a, b (distinct valid indices), minutes (1..100). Links are undirected; no duplicate unordered endpoint pair. At most 28 links.
Find a route from from to to using links. Minimize total travel minutes. For equal total minutes, prefer fewer links, then the lexicographically smaller full node sequence, so equally fast trips require fewer junction decisions. A full node sequence includes both endpoints; compare integer node sequences using ordinary lexicographic order.
Return exactly {"route":[node,...],"minutes":integer}, or {"route":[],"minutes":null} if unreachable. Staying at the starting node costs zero: {"nodes":1,"links":[],"from":0,"to":0} returns {"route":[0],"minutes":0}.

Extend the botanical-garden walking-route CLI to avoid temporarily blocked links. Implement main.py as a Python 3.12 standard-library CLI: one strict JSON value on stdin, one JSON value on stdout, no diagnostics on stdout. Numbers must use integer JSON syntax. Reject malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, noninteger numbers, and any schema violation with exactly {"error":"invalid"}; booleans are not integers. Reject missing or extra fields at every object level. The supplied source is a fresh canonical starter, not a previous completed submission. Implement this milestone's complete behavior in run(value); keep strict parsing. Use no dependencies.
Input has exactly {"nodes":integer,"links":[...],"from":integer,"to":integer,"blocked":[...]}. nodes is 1..8 and defines indices 0..nodes-1; from and to are valid indices. Each of at most 28 undirected links has exactly integer a, b (distinct valid indices), minutes (1..100), with no duplicate unordered pair. Each blocked item is a two-element array of valid integer node indices naming an existing link in either direction; no duplicate unordered blocked pair, at most 28 items.
Remove blocked links before finding a route. Minimize total travel minutes. Keep the established tie policy for equally fast routes. A route lists all traversed nodes, including both endpoints.
Return exactly {"route":[node,...],"minutes":integer}, or {"route":[],"minutes":null} if unreachable. Staying at the starting node costs zero: {"nodes":1,"links":[],"from":0,"to":0,"blocked":[]} returns {"route":[0],"minutes":0}.

Input has exactly {"nodes":integer,"links":[...],"from":integer,"to":integer,"blocked":[...],"via":integer}. nodes is 1..8; from, to, via and link endpoints are indices 0..nodes-1. Each of at most 28 undirected links has exactly integer a, b (distinct valid indices), minutes (1..100), with no duplicate unordered endpoint pair. Each blocked item is a two-element array of valid integer indices naming an existing link in either direction; no duplicate unordered blocked pair, at most 28 items.
Remove blocked links. Find a route from from to to visiting via at least once, including an endpoint visit. Nodes and links may be revisited when needed. Minimize total travel minutes.
